## Reader and narrative

- [ ] A first-time, non-technical reader can state why the lesson matters.
- [ ] The opening situation, complication, and resolution are clear.
- [ ] The story supports the evidence without invented drama, quotes, or facts.
- [ ] Technical terms are defined close to first use.

## Writing review

- [ ] Round 1 residue scan passed.
- [ ] Round 2 style-pattern scan passed.
- [ ] Round 3 spoken edit completed.
- [ ] Round 4 independent edit completed.
- [ ] Round 5 skeptical fact review completed.
- [ ] Round 6 record-boundary review completed.
- [ ] Final rendered-page proofread completed.

## Evidence

- [ ] Claims are labeled in notes as established, current, emerging, disputed,
      or speculative.
- [ ] Primary or official sources support the central claims.
- [ ] Contradicting evidence and important limits were checked.
- [ ] Time-sensitive claims include a date, version, or other boundary.
- [ ] Data and models include provenance, license, and affected-group concerns
      when relevant.

## Code and interface

- [ ] Every published code chunk ran without cached output.
- [ ] Important outputs have assertions.
- [ ] Tidyverse style check passed.
- [ ] Row-level outputs retain their source IDs; every collapse or flattening
      step answers an explicit corpus-wide question.
- [ ] Model selection and tuning stay inside training data; final test data is
      opened only after the candidate and settings are fixed.
- [ ] Unsupervised parameters are checked with more than one predeclared
      diagnostic before outputs are interpreted.
- [ ] The full site rendered without unexplained warnings or errors.
- [ ] Links, keyboard navigation, focus, zoom, and small screens were checked.
- [ ] Periodic-table tests passed when its data, links, or styles changed.
